title: Volume 1 Chapter 4: Candy Coating & Brush Painting 1
content: "So, I was talking to Karla about the nails for the shoot..."
One day during lunch break.
I was once again consulting with Sayori on the school rooftop. Of course, it was about nails.
"I thought it would be great if we matched the nails on both hands and feet! What do you think, Azuma-kun? Are you okay with that?"
"Yeah, I think I can manage—probably."
Sayori, despite being close and chatty in class, never brings up nail topics.
She believes that I might get taken away by my friends.
However, she accidentally showed my pedicure to her model friend named Karla, resulting in one more customer for me.
That said, they were already good friends.
Now, it seems they’re discussing what kind of nails would be good for the weekend shoot.
"Well, I want to use glitter lame powder!"
"Glitter...?"
"This! It's the kind you can find at a hundred yen shop!"
Sayori pulled out a round plastic case. Inside was a shimmering golden powder.
"For example, if we mix this into the top coat!"
"So, we can create a different expression while keeping the base intact."
"Exactly! Wait!? You figured that out just by looking at it!?"
"Well, I had a good idea."
The layering technique is something I’ve used in plastic model painting as well.
"Um, the image I have is... like, in the night sky, golden stars shining brightly, and then bam—sparkle! Wow, it's just so beautiful!"
"Your vocabulary..."
That's almost just onomatopoeia.
However, I understood what she wanted to convey. In short, she wanted nails that looked like a starry sky using this powder.
"I think there are various ways to do it, but I want to go with that this time! I want it to feel like stars floating against a night backdrop!"
Sayori giggled.
It was clear that this was her favorite idea born from discussions with her friends.
"I see. So instead of mixing this powder into the base paint, you want to mix it with a transparent top coat to create a sense of depth."
"Yes, exactly!"
Sayori nodded eagerly.
Despite her limited vocabulary, she seemed happy that her intentions were getting across.
"Are you okay with layering? Is it your strong suit?"
"I'm not a pro... but I've done it before. Layering transparent paint can give depth and change the texture. There's also candy coating."
"Candy... like candy?"
Sayori tilted her head.
"Um, layering transparent paint as a base—no, it’s probably faster to show you."
I operated my smartphone and pulled up examples of plastic models online.

The screen displayed a plastic model using candy coating. The entire figure was enveloped in a glossy metallic sheen. With a mirror finish, it was shiny enough that if you looked closely, you could see your reflection.
"Whoa!? This is amazing! Is this made of metal? Can plastic models do this!?"
"No, it's still a 'plastic model.' It's made of plastic."
"But it looks so shiny!"
"That's candy coating. First, you paint the base, then apply transparent paint several times, and finally polish it with compound to get this result. It looks like a candy apple, right?"
"Candy apple... oh, so that's why it's called candy!?"
"Exactly."
Sayori smiled, having understood. What a straightforward person.
"Wow, it looks like metal, though..."
"The texture can change completely with paint. You can create a matte finish for realism or use weathering techniques to make it look rusty or scratched..."
"Wow, that's amazing! So Azuma-kun really is a professional painter!?"
"No, I'm just an amateur..."
There might be a path to becoming a professional modeler, but my skills and effort still have a long way to go.
"Hmm, but I see... so it's not made of metal."
"Sometimes, you might use commercially available metal parts, but basically, it's all about plastic processing, so I haven't really done much metal work..."
Making a robot out of metal sounds fun, but that’s no longer a plastic model.
"If you could do it, I was thinking of asking you to make earrings..."
"Earrings!?"
I’ve never even touched one, let alone made it.
As my nail skills improved, I could feel Sayori's requests becoming more demanding.
At first, she was hesitant, but now, with the expectation and trust that "Azuma-kun can do this too," the level of her orders was rising.
While that was a nice thing, it also—
"Well, earrings are a bit much."
"Oh, I'm sorry! Let's focus on nails first!"
"Well, I think using this glitter powder for the nails should be fine."
"Yay! As expected of Azuma-kun! This will really boost the mood for the shoot!"
Even though we hadn’t started painting yet, Sayori exaggeratedly expressed her joy.
It seemed that Sayori dressed up, particularly for her own motivation and mood elevation.
Especially since she loved looking at hands, doing nails must have a strong impact on her mental state.
(...Well, it’s probably similar to how I feel when I successfully paint something.)
I wasn’t sure if it was appropriate to compare the two.
I recalled the excitement of successfully completing my first candy coating.
When I sprayed a thick layer of clear coat as a base, polished it with compound, and achieved a shiny, mirror-like finish, the feeling was probably similar.
"Alright, I’ll head to the garage with Karla today."
"Okay. Thanks!"
"Do you think we can finish the nails today?"
"Probably—should be fine. Worst case, we can use tomorrow too."
"Got it. We should be able to make it in time for the shoot."
It seemed she was coming with a friend today.
The model named Karla, whom I saw in a fashion magazine, had four arms and blue skin, which was striking, but otherwise looked just like a human.
I had gotten quite used to nails by now. Even with four arms, I could wrap up candy coating fairly quickly.
"See you later after school!"
Sayori gulped down her bread without chewing, which might be a dragon's habit.
I waved goodbye to Sayori as she left the rooftop, her tail swaying behind her.
(I might end up with some strange rumors again, so I should wait a bit before heading back to class.)
If it got out that we were eating lunch together on the rooftop, people would start making weird assumptions.
Besides, I was an introvert and shy, so I couldn’t even imagine being in a romantic relationship with Sayori—
(Friends, huh...)
I was actually a bit nervous about being introduced to Sayori's friends, being a natural social awkward.
But well, since I was coming to do nails, it should be fine.
I could just work as usual. I didn’t have to talk while working.
(Calm down, calm down...)
I had gotten used to nails, so it would be over quickly.
The technique for candy coating wasn’t that difficult—I thought so at that moment.
But I would come to realize that was a mistake when I met Sayori's friend, Karla.
That afternoon, I prepared my tools in the garage.
Nails using glitter powder.
Since I needed to mix paint, I laid out the paint tray and brushes.
Sayori had said she would be a bit late because she was meeting up with her friend.
(That was quick preparation.)
I already had all the tools for nails, so there wasn’t much to do beforehand.
Should I clean up? After all, a girl was coming—
"Girls..."
I recalled.
The other day, when Sayori held my hand in this garage.
Well, I always touched her hands during nail work, but—
She had firmly held both of my hands and said,
"I really like your hands, Azuma-kun."
Remembering Sayori's words, I couldn’t help but stare at my own hands. I felt my face heat up as I recalled her warmth.
I knew it wasn’t in a romantic sense.
(Girls are really troublesome...!)
Was it because she was a gal or because she was Sayori?
I didn’t know, but it was a fact that she was disturbing my peace of mind.
(Alright, focus, focus.)
I had to do nails soon, so how could I feel this way?
"...Oh, by the way."
I hadn’t made a plastic model in a while. Of course, I had bought new kits, but my head was filled with Sayori's nails, and they had been piling up.
I was accepting paid plastic model commissions online. I couldn’t neglect that either. When I checked my phone, I saw several requests had come in through the order site.
(Maybe I should do some... It might help me concentrate.)
I went to the back storage and brought out the kit I had been commissioned to create.
I opened the box and took out the runners.
For today, I could just do a simple assembly. The sound of cutting plastic echoed in the garage as I snapped the parts out.
I cut the parts from the runners, lightly sanded the gates, and then assembled the parts according to the instructions.
I was getting the hang of it.
Recent kits had good proportions and sufficient mobility. Even without painting, the color separation was well done, and the parts structure was simple.
(Well, I also enjoy modifying the older, harder-to-assemble kits...)
Until now, I had always done this alone in silence. But.
If Sayori were watching, she would probably say "Wow, that's amazing!" even for this simple repetitive task.
(Ah, come on! Lately, I keep thinking about her...!)
Am I really seeking praise just for assembling parts?
It felt like my alone time was being completely invaded by her. Because she—she praises me for everything.
I needed to change my mindset.
If a beautiful girl said she liked me, it would confuse anyone. Because I’m an introvert. But she only likes my skills as a modeler.
Then I should just focus on being a craftsman.
I continued cutting and assembling the parts.
In no time, a plastic model was completed. It was a simple assembly—just made according to the instructions, but I managed to finish it in about an hour, which was quite good.
To respond to the online requests, I would think about the direction for modifications and painting, but for a casual task, this was perfect.
(I really love plastic models.)
Even though it was a simple assembly kit, I nodded in satisfaction as I looked at the finished product.
My mind, which had been confused because of Sayori, had completely calmed down through the process of making the model. It was a kind of meditation.
